data.title: Westwater Updates Battery-Grade Graphite Strategy and Progress
data.description:
Westwater Resources ( (WWR) ) has provided an announcement.

On September 14, 2026, Westwater Resources’ Executive Chairman Terence Cryan presented the company’s updated business plan at the H.C. Wainwright 28th Annual Global Investment Conference, coinciding with the posting of an investor presentation on its website. The materials highlighted Westwater’s progress on its Kellyton Graphite Plant, where more than half of the planned $245 million capital cost has been invested and an EXIM loan approved, as well as its broader mine-to-market graphite strategy centered on U.S. battery demand.

The update underscored that Phase 1 of the Kellyton facility is designed to provide 12,500 mtpa of battery-grade natural graphite, with Phase 2 expected to lift capacity to 50,000 mtpa, supported by ongoing customer qualification and offtake discussions. By advancing a strategically located, vertically integrated graphite operation at a time when the U.S. imports all battery-grade natural graphite and relies heavily on Chinese supply, the company is seeking to strengthen its industry positioning and appeal to stakeholders focused on domestic, secure battery-materials sourcing.

data.description:

data.title: South Korea’s Import Cost Surge Cools Sharply
data.description:
South Korea’s import prices rose 15.6% year on year, slowing sharply from the previous 18.7% increase. The pace of import inflation is lower by 3.1 percentage points, signaling easing cost pressures compared with the prior reading.

The 15.6% gain in import prices undershot analysts’ 23.0% estimate, reinforcing expectations for more contained inflation and slightly reduced pressure on the Bank of Korea’s policy stance. Equity markets are likely to view the downside surprise as supportive for rate-sensitive sectors such as financials and consumer stocks, while exporters may see a more muted reaction as import cost relief feeds through gradually rather than as an immediate sentiment shock.

data.title: Meridian Energy reports record demand and strong hydro storage in August
data.description:
Meridian Energy Limited ( (NZ:MEL) ) has provided an update.

Meridian Energy has released its August 2026 operating report, highlighting that New Zealand reached a record peak electricity demand early in the month, which was met comfortably through high renewable generation and North Island battery support. The company reports robust hydro and snow storage across its key catchments, bolstered by El Niño-driven inflows that leave national hydro storage at 155% of historical average and South Island storage at 178%.

Operational metrics show August was warm and wet, particularly in the South Island, with national electricity demand down 0.3% year on year and demand over the last 12 months 3.2% higher than the previous period. Meridian’s retail sales volumes fell 4.7% compared with August 2025, with declines across most customer segments except large business, while NZAS load rose to 578MW, underscoring strong industrial demand despite softer overall retail volumes.
